summary: Over 14 days, CGM coverage is good and time in range is high, but time below range is 5.1 percent and clusters at 19:00 local and overnight. Carbs are undeclared and unlogged, so UAM and SMB plus Dynamic ISF explain afternoon highs and later insulin on board. No isolated profile or AAPS number change is supported; keep the current profile and verify late-day intake against bedtime IOB before any single later lever.

analysis_steps.findings: Nightscout coverage is 98.7 percent over 14 days with a 5-minute cadence, 10 gaps, and a largest gap of 65 minutes. The selected AAPS profile is complete and declared historically applicable. Insulin is logged (655 insulin entries, 275.95 U) while carbs, extended carbs, and meal-strategy objects are zero or empty. Closed-loop temps and SMB therefore dominate observed glucose more than a pure scheduled-basal test.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3995 valid CGM entries; treatment_summary carb_entries 0 and total_carbs_g 0.0; carb_treatment_entries empty; meal_strategies empty; strategy_stable_for_period null; profile_context historical_applicability yes; scheduled basal sums to 16.2 U/day.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No meal times or composition; activity not coded; u200 dilute conversion not quantified; included treatments are a subset of 2315.

analysis_steps.findings: Mean glucose 121.6 mg/dL and TIR 86.0 percent look strong, but TBR 5.1 percent and CV 32.6 percent are the binding safety limits. Local TBR peaks at 01:00 (18.5 percent) and 19:00 (15.3 percent). TAR peaks at 16:00 local (32.1 percent). Extreme lows of 41-42 mg/dL sit in the late-afternoon to evening cluster plus one isolated morning low. Sampled IOB reached about 4.7-5.9 U after UAM or DynISF chasing.
analysis_steps.evidence: glucose_summary; hourly_glucose_local; glucose_extremes; therapy_response_windows with large 2-4 hour drops after afternoon corrections; loop IOB 4.73 U and 5.935 U.
analysis_steps.dependencies: data_quality carb gap and dilution uncertainty.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No rescue-carb or hypo-treatment markers; no meter confirmation of CGM lows.

analysis_steps.findings: 05:00-08:00 local is the cleanest fasting-like window (TIR 95-99 percent) under basal 0.7-0.8 U/h. Overnight averages are low-normal with excess TBR under basal 0.6 U/h and target 90 mg/dL. The 16:00 basal 0.5 U/h sits under the TAR peak, but unlogged meals, UAM, and afternoon TTs remain plausible. 18:00-19:00 is a crash after the afternoon peak, so raising afternoon insulin is not isolated as safe. Closed loop frequently zeros or raises temps, so scheduled basal is not the delivered rate.
analysis_steps.evidence: hourly_glucose_local; basal_segments 0.6/0.7/0.8/0.7/0.5/0.6/0.7 U/h; targets 90/100/90 mg/dL; representative temp basals including 0 U/h and about 2-4 U/h; TTs to 135 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.dependencies: safety_overview TBR brake; data_quality no fasting meal-free day.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Cannot split 23:00-03:00 IOB into basal versus SMB/UAM versus corrections; first days may precede the 13 Aug profile-switch notes even though applicability is declared yes.

analysis_steps.findings: CR cannot be validated because no carb treatments exist. Flat ISF 56 mg/dL/U is only an anchor; sampled variable_sens ranged about 28-124 mg/dL/U with DynISF on. DIA 10 h is long enough to carry afternoon IOB into the overnight TBR window but is not proven too long or too short. Correction windows are contaminated by UAM, temps, and unknown intake.
analysis_steps.evidence: carb_ratio_segments 13/11.1/13.2/10.5/12.6 g/U; isf 56 mg/dL/U; dia_hours 10; 24 correction-only therapy windows; cob 0 in sampled statuses.
analysis_steps.dependencies: basal_targets evening crash; safety_overview against strengthening ISF or CR.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No paired carb and bolus events; insulin peak not supplied; dilution versus displayed units unknown.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are on, SMB is always enabled, and COB-based SMB flags are off. That matches zero carbs and cob 0: UAM is the meal controller, not duplicate COB counting. Interval 3 min and 15/20 min SMB windows, plus custom UAM boost language, can deliver material meal insulin (sampled microboluses 0.05-0.4 U and one 1.6 U UAM high boost). Night statuses more often suspend than fill a basal hole.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_enabled true; uam_enabled true; smb_always_enabled true; smb_with_cob_enabled false; sampled reasons with UAM Boost and insulinReq up to 2.59 U; enacted rates capped near 4 U/h.

analysis_steps.data_gaps: Custom boost logic is not an inventory field; full SMB stream is not included.

analysis_steps.findings: Autosens is off; a sensitivity_ratio of 1 is a neutral current adjustment, not proof of disabled Autosens. DynISF at 70 percent is the delivered ISF at highs and can explain afternoon catch-up plus later overshoot. Max basal 12 U/h and max IOB 25 U are far above TDD about 20 U and sampled IOB peaks; they did not bind this period. Carb-absorption settings had no COB to act on.

analysis_steps.data_gaps: Cannot separate DynISF effect from UAM timing without meal logs.

analysis_steps.findings: User-declared meal_strategies is an empty list and strategy_stable_for_period is null, so no prebolus minutes or immediate bolus percent exist to reproduce. Observed execution matches that declaration: only correction boluses and UAM/SMB. Morning rises have little TBR; the 14:00-19:00 local cluster is high then crash. Adding a carb bolus or invented prebolus would stack on current UAM.

analysis_steps.findings: No e-carb amount, start offset, or duration is declared or logged. E-carbs are not a pump extended bolus, and no extended-carb duration should be inferred. Absorption settings did not create phantom COB. Afternoon multi-hour rises are not a measured carb-absorption curve.

analysis_steps.findings: Ranked explanation: unannounced intake drives UAM/SMB and DynISF at highs, leaving 2-6 U IOB that lands on target 90 mg/dL and DIA 10 h between 18:00 and 03:00 local. Afternoon TAR is not isolated as a 16:00 basal defect. Overnight TBR is not isolated as a 00:00 basal defect versus leftover IOB versus target 90. Package overrides any earlier impulse to change CR, ISF, SMB delivery, or DynISF together. Safe order is keep the profile, keep automation, and collect meal-clock plus bedtime IOB evidence before selecting one later lever.
analysis_steps.evidence: TBR 5.1 percent; local 16:00 TAR 32.1 percent versus 19:00 TBR 15.3 percent; cob 0; DynISF variable_sens compressed at highs and weaker near target; max IOB not binding; empty declared meal plan.
analysis_steps.dependencies: All prior stages; do not change dependent insulin settings in one step.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Nights with low evening IOB versus high UAM IOB are not labeled in the package.

strengths: CGM completeness is good enough for hourly local-time review.
Overall TIR 86.0 percent with mean 121.6 mg/dL.
05:00-08:00 local fasting-like control is strong (TIR 95-99 percent).
Overnight TAR is near zero; hyperglycemia is clustered, not all day.
Autosens target-lowering is already off while TBR is the safety brake.
High afternoon temporary targets were already used as a way to slow insulin rather than add meal insulin.
issues: Time below range 5.1 percent, with 01:00 local TBR 18.5 percent and 19:00 local TBR 15.3 percent.
Recurring afternoon rise then evening crash, including CGM lows of 41-42 mg/dL.
No carb entries and empty declared meal strategies, so CR and e-carbs cannot be tested.
UAM/SMB plus DynISF are substituting for meal announcement and can leave high IOB.
Overnight target 90 mg/dL, DIA 10 h, and leftover IOB are not yet separable from 00:00 basal 0.6 U/h.
Max IOB 25 U and max basal 12 U/h did not cause the pattern but are far above observed TDD and would not tightly limit a bad UAM run.

recommendations.title: Keep the profile and separate leftover IOB from overnight landing
recommendations.description: Overnight TBR is real, but meals, UAM/SMB, DynISF-at-highs, DIA 10 h, target 90 mg/dL, and 00:00 basal 0.6 U/h can all produce the same lows. The package does not isolate a profile number. The first safe action is to keep every profile segment and compare bedtime IOB after logged late-day intake versus quieter evenings.

recommendations.title: Leave SMB, UAM, and DynISF unchanged until meal clocks exist
recommendations.description: Automation is the current meal bolus. Tightening delivery or DynISF in the same step as any profile change would stack effects. Disabling UAM without announcement would leave the 14:00-16:00 local rise unmanaged. This only sets the action order: automation review comes after the meal-clock check, and then at most one lever.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep overnight target 90 mg/dL, daytime target 100 mg/dL, and every other profile segment unchanged.
profile_recommendation.rationale: The only profile-like safety signal is overnight and late-evening TBR, but DynISF is weaker near target and sampled nights show the loop suspending, which points to leftover afternoon IOB more than a proven 00:00 basal or ISF error. Changing target, basal, ISF, or DIA now would confound the unlogged-meal explanation.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Log clock time for 3 late-afternoon eating events and bedtime IOB, then compare overnight TBR on those nights versus nights with low evening IOB.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: 00:00-03:00 local averages 90-106 mg/dL with TBR 10-18 percent. Uncertainty: leftover UAM IOB and target 90 mg/dL can cause the same lows. Dependencies: do not change with target, DIA, or SMB delivery.

Evidence: 05:00-07:00 local TIR 95-99 percent and low TBR aside from one 42 mg/dL incident. Uncertainty: that isolated low is not a repeating 05:00 defect. Dependencies: morning window is not the binding safety problem.

Evidence: 06:00-08:00 local remains high TIR with almost no TAR. Uncertainty: loop temps still override the schedule. Dependencies: keep unless a fasting no-meal morning set shows a rise or fall attributable to this step only.

Evidence: 09:00-13:00 local rise and TAR coincide with likely breakfast or lunch plus UAM. Uncertainty: not a clean basal signal. Dependencies: unused CR and always-on SMB can fully explain this window.

Evidence: this is the lowest basal under the 16:00 local TAR peak of 32.1 percent. Uncertainty: unlogged meals and UAM remain more likely than a basal hole. Dependencies: raising this segment together with SMB or DynISF would increase 19:00 crash risk.

Evidence: 18:00 local already has TBR 7.7 percent after the afternoon peak. Uncertainty: activity, GLP-1 notes, and stacked IOB are not coded. Dependencies: any increase conflicts with the 19:00 hypo cluster.

Evidence: 19:00 local TBR 15.3 percent and CGM lows of 41 mg/dL. Uncertainty: this is the overshoot window, not a proven under-basal window. Dependencies: withhold change until afternoon UAM IOB is measured.
Evidence: zero carb treatments, so this CR never fired. Uncertainty: overnight carbs are not shown. Dependencies: CR change is blocked until meals are announced.
Evidence: no carb entries in the night or dawn window. Uncertainty: the stronger ratio would only matter if overnight carbs appear. Dependencies: unused while cob stays 0.
Evidence: morning TAR exists but no meal boluses used this CR. Uncertainty: UAM catch-up is the observed tool. Dependencies: do not infer a weaker or stronger CR from unannounced rises.

Evidence: strongest CR sits on the same clock as peak TAR and the 18:00-19:00 crash, but it was unused. Uncertainty: if announcement starts, this segment is the most hypo-sensitive. Dependencies: keep until logged meals exist; do not pair a CR change with SMB.
Evidence: evening TBR with cob 0 is not a CR test. Uncertainty: any future evening carb entry would land on leftover IOB. Dependencies: meal announcement first.

Evidence: delivered sensitivity is DynISF (variable_sens about 28-124), not static 56. Uncertainty: u200 labeling may change the meaning of 56. Dependencies: do not change ISF in the same step as DynISF factor, SMB, or basal.

Evidence: overnight TBR occurs on a 90 mg/dL target and is the most proximal landing setting. Uncertainty: leftover IOB may be sufficient without a target error. Dependencies: changing target together with basal or DIA would hide the IOB-source test.

Evidence: daytime target 100 mg/dL aligns with the safer morning band and some afternoon TTs already go to 135 mg/dL. Uncertainty: afternoon TAR is meal-shaped. Dependencies: not the overnight TBR lever.

Evidence: target returns to 90 mg/dL at 23:00 as glucose is still settling and TBR is 6-10 percent. Uncertainty: same IOB-versus-target confound as 00:00. Dependencies: keep with profile.target.00_00; do not move only one overnight target segment.

Evidence: DIA 10 h can keep afternoon SMB active into 23:00-03:00, matching overnight TBR. Uncertainty: no clean no-food IOB decay or insulin peak is available. Dependencies: changing DIA with SMB or ISF would double-count the same IOB story.

Evidence: cob 0 and empty meal plan mean UAM is the meal path. Uncertainty: turning UAM off would leave afternoon TAR without a replacement announcement method. Dependencies: keep while CR stays unused; no source component is null so verify is not used.

Evidence: flags match zero COB and allow high-TT lockout, which was already used. Uncertainty: late TTs may be too late for the 19:00 crash. Dependencies: activation is consistent; delivery, not these switches, is the later suspicion.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: enacted rates were multiplier-capped near 4 U/h and sampled IOB peaked near 6 U, so 12 U/h and 25 U did not bind. Uncertainty: the wide ceiling is a runaway risk, not the 14-day cause. Dependencies: changing limits would not test basal, CR, or meal timing.

Evidence: DynISF 70 percent compresses ISF at highs and is part of the chase; Autosens off is appropriate while TBR is 5.1 percent. Uncertainty: factor 70 percent versus UAM timing is not separable. Dependencies: do not enable target lowering or change this with profile ISF or SMB delivery.

Evidence: no carbs and cob 0, so these settings had no job and did not create double COB. Uncertainty: they would only matter after announcement. Dependencies: unused; keep rather than verify because values are present.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Keep the observed plan: no declared prebolus, no immediate bolus percent, no e-carbs, and meal insulin only from always-on SMB plus UAM. Do not add a carb-based bolus or e-carb layer on top of that path. If late-day food is known, the file already shows higher temporary targets rather than extra meal insulin.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Declared meal_strategies is empty and Nightscout shows 0 g carbs, so user declaration and execution agree on unannounced intake. The recurring 14:00-19:00 local high-then-crash matches UAM and DynISF IOB, not a missing prebolus number.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Record clock time for 3 late-afternoon eating events and whether any insulin besides SMB was given, then keep the next 6 hours of CGM and bedtime IOB.

exceptions.suggestion: Same unannounced UAM path, with no stacked corrections or new e-carbs in this window
exceptions.rationale: Highest TAR then 19:00 TBR 15.3 percent and the extreme lows live here.

exceptions.suggestion: Same UAM-only approach; do not invent a morning prebolus or CR change
exceptions.rationale: Rise and TAR occur with TBR near 0, so catch-up is less costly than in the evening.

implementation_steps: Treat this as decision-support only. Independently verify every idea with the care team and change at most one dependent setting, then watch glucose closely.
Keep the current profile (basal, CR, ISF, DIA, targets) as the baseline.
Keep SMB, UAM, activation flags, delivery numbers, DynISF, Autosens-off, and carb-absorption settings unchanged during the observation step.
For 3 late-afternoon eating events, write the clock time, whether any non-SMB insulin was given, bedtime IOB, and the next 6 hours of CGM.
Compare overnight TBR on those nights versus quieter evenings before discussing a single later lever (overnight landing versus SMB delivery versus DynISF factor).
If a later review occurs, do not move profile ISF and DynISF, or basal and target, or SMB delivery and meal announcement, in the same step.
education: Time in range can look strong while time below range is still the setting that should limit insulin increases.
When carbs are not entered, UAM is a rise detector, not a second carb counter, and cob 0 is expected.
Dynamic ISF can make the listed ISF of 56 mg/dL/U much stronger at high glucose and weaker near target, so lows after a peak often reflect insulin already on board.
A sensitivity_ratio of 1 is a neutral current adjustment, not a sign that Autosens is turned off.
E-carbs are a carb-absorption forecast, not a pump extended bolus, and cannot be inferred from an empty extended-carb average.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. It is not medical advice and does not change AAPS automatically.
The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
Time below range 5.1 percent, including 41-42 mg/dL readings, is the binding constraint against adding meal insulin or strengthening afternoon delivery.
Max IOB 25 U and max basal 12 U/h are much larger than total daily insulin near 20 U and would not tightly stop a bad UAM or DynISF run.
Site changes, sensor changes, an occlusion and pump error on 19 Aug, and GLP-1 1.25 mg notes can distort single days and should not be treated as basal proof.
